tools.name: list-connections
tools.description: List all configured SSH profiles and their connection status. Use this to discover available hosts before running commands.

tools.name: list-sessions
tools.description: List active sessions for a given SSH profile.

tools.name: open-session
tools.description: Open a named session on a remote host. Use type="interactive" for stateful shell (CWD/env persists between commands) or type="background" for long-running processes.

name.description: Session name (alphanumeric, dash, underscore, max 64 chars)

ttlMs.description: Idle timeout for THIS session in ms (the profile default applies when omitted). May shorten the profile timeout; may lengthen it only up to sessionBackgroundMaxMs for a background session, or not at all for an interactive one

tools.name: close-session
tools.description: Close a named session. A background session's command is signalled on the host (INT, then TERM, then KILL) before its channel is dropped; an interactive session's shell is ended. The response says so if the command could not be signalled or had not stopped in time.

tools.name: read-session-output
tools.description: Read recent output from a background session (e.g., tail -f logs).

lines.description: Number of recent lines to read

tools.name: read-command
tools.description: Execute a READ-ONLY command from an allowlist (ls, cat, grep, find, stat, df, etc.). This tool does NOT modify the system. Prefer this tool for all read operations. Single-line only: a command containing a line break is refused, so upload a multi-line script with sftp-upload and run it by path.

command.description: Read-only shell command (must be in the allowlist)

tools.name: run-command
tools.description: Execute an arbitrary shell command on the remote server. May modify the system. Commands classified destructive or privileged go through the approval gate; approvalPolicy on the profile decides whether that is a prompt, an automatic allow, or a refusal. Single-line only: a command containing a line break is refused, so upload a multi-line script with sftp-upload and run it by path.

session.description: Run in an existing interactive session (stateful)

tools.name: privileged-command
tools.description: Execute a command with sudo elevation. Goes through the approval gate; approvalPolicy on the profile decides whether that is a prompt, an automatic allow, or a refusal. The sudo password is piped via stdin for the prompt only (never visible in process list); the command itself runs with stdin at /dev/null, so it can never read the password back. Single-line only: a command containing a line break is refused, so upload a multi-line script with sftp-upload and run it by path.

tools.name: signal-process
tools.description: Send a signal (INT, TERM, KILL) to a remote process by PID.

tools.name: sftp-upload
tools.description: Upload a file to the remote server via SFTP (secure file transfer, not shell-based). Replaces an existing file at that path unconditionally — there is no overwrite flag and no way to require a new destination.

remotePath.description: Remote file path. No leading or trailing whitespace, and no control, bidirectional or zero-width characters: the approval prompt and the audit record quote this path back.

tools.name: sftp-download
tools.description: Download a file from the remote server via SFTP.

remotePath.description: Remote file path. No leading or trailing whitespace, and no control, bidirectional or zero-width characters: the approval prompt and the audit record quote this path back.

tools.name: sftp-list
tools.description: List a remote directory over SFTP, with a bounded number of entries and a bounded response size. Read-only.

remotePath.description: Remote directory to list. No leading or trailing whitespace, and no control, bidirectional or zero-width characters.

maxEntries.description: Max entries to return (default 200, hard cap 1000)

tools.name: sftp-upload-file
tools.description: Upload a local file to the remote host over SFTP, streaming it without passing the contents through model context. The local file must be inside the transferRoot directory the operator configured; without that setting this tool refuses. Use this for binary or large files; use sftp-upload for short text you already have.

localPath.description: Local file to upload, inside defaults.transferRoot

remotePath.description: Remote destination path. No leading or trailing whitespace, and no control, bidirectional or zero-width characters.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing remote file (default false)

mode.description: Remote file mode, 1 to 511 (0o777); setuid, setgid and the sticky bit are refused. e.g. 420 for 0644. Omit for 0600 on a new file, or the replaced file’s permission bits.

tools.name: sftp-download-file
tools.description: Download a remote file to local disk over SFTP, streaming it without passing the contents through model context. The destination must be inside the transferRoot directory the operator configured; without that setting this tool refuses. Use this for binary or large files; use sftp-download when you need to read the contents.

remotePath.description: Remote file to download. No leading or trailing whitespace, and no control, bidirectional or zero-width characters.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing local file (default false)

tools.name: reload-config
tools.description: Report or reload the server's config file. action="status" (the default) shows the config path, when it was loaded, the sha256 of its bytes and the result of the last reload; never the contents. action="reload" re-reads the file, validates it exactly as startup does, and applies it only if every check passes; a refused reload changes nothing. Command-line flags are never reloaded. Applying closes connections, with their sessions, whose profile was removed or whose connection fields changed, and clears approval grants.

action.description: "status" (default) reports the loaded config; "reload" re-reads and applies the file

resources.name: connections
resources.description: List all SSH profiles and their connection status
